rationale: Hebrews 6:13 reports the oath of Genesis 22:16 ('He swore by Himself', BSB; 'By Myself I have sworn' in 22:16, the only verse in this app's BSB Genesis with 'By Myself') and 6:14 introduces the promise with 'saying' (λέγων). The Greek of 6:14, read on Bible Hub, 'εὐλογῶν εὐλογήσω σε καὶ πληθύνων πληθυνῶ σε', matches the Swete Septuagint of 22:17 ('εὐλογῶν εὐλογήσω σε, καὶ πληθύνων πληθυνῶ τὸ σπέρμα σου') except that Hebrews has 'you' where Genesis has 'your seed' (a Greek difference; the BSB of Hebrews 6:14 reads 'multiply your descendants'). The opening particle splits by edition: Swete's Septuagint ('εἰ μήν') and Nestle and Westcott-Hort ('Εἰ μὴν') against the Byzantine text and Textus Receptus ('Ἦ μὴν'). Barnes and the Cambridge Bible refer the passage to Genesis 22:16-17, and Meyer gives the Septuagint wording of 22:16. Graded quotation because an introducing word and near-verbatim wording are both present (the standard the Genesis 15 rows use), and explicit because only one Old Testament scene joins a divine oath by Himself to these words; the one-word change is reported, not hidden.
